claim:
Text: "The Wire called Durga puja racist and the goddess Durga a sex worker"
Claim date: October 26, 2020
before_justification: The fact-check reveals that the viral claim misrepresents a 2016 [report by The Wire](https://thewire.in/92853/smriti-irani-reads-out-obscene-verse-in-lok-sabha-to-show-jnu-event-was-not-about-culture/) covering a parliamentary speech by then-HRD Minister Smriti Irani, who read excerpts from a controversial pamphlet. The statements about Durga being a "sex worker" and Durga Puja being "racist" were direct quotations from that pamphlet, not The Wire’s own editorial stance, as confirmed by multiple fact-checkers ([Alt News](https://www.altnews.in/the-wire-did-not-disrespect-durga-excerpt-from-2016-article-misrepresented/), [The Quint](https://www.thequint.com/news/webqoof/excerpt-shared-without-context-to-label-the-wire-as-anti-hindu), [The Logical Indian](https://thelogicalindian.com/fact-check/wire-demeans-goddess-durga-24521)). The Wire’s founding editor also clarified that the article was quoting the speech, not endorsing the content, and that the screenshot was taken out of context.
after_justification: The claim is refuted because the viral screenshot was cropped; the original 2016 article by [The Wire](https://www.boomlive.in/fake-news/cropped-screenshot-of-the-wire-article-on-durga-puja-is-misleading-10354) was reporting on a quote from Smriti Irani reading from a pamphlet, not making those assertions directly.

The screenshot is being shared as several parts of India are celebrating Durga puja and Navratri, both festivals celebrating the goddess Durga.
The same cropped screenshot is viral with captions on Twitter.

An excerpt from an article in The Wire is making the rounds on Twitter to claim that the news organisation promoted ‘anti-Hindu’ sentiments by terming Durga Puja a “racist festival” and the Hindu deity a “sex worker”.
Ex-navy officer Harinder Sikka questioned The Wire in a critically worded tweet, “Can u dare write such obscene words for Islam?”
Twitter handle @missionkaali followed by Delhi BJP leader Kapil Mishra also shared the screenshot speculating if the outlet indeed published the excerpt.
Several other users — @Voice_Of_Dharma, @Muralik79739498 — posted the screenshot. Twitter handle @indianrightwing opined, “Maa durga being called a s*x worker that too during navratri by
@thewire_in. There can be no punishment except for legal death sentence…”
Twitter handle @indianrightwing which suggested the “death penalty” for The Wire as punishment for alleged “Hinduphobic” views also shared the article containing the excerpt in question.
Had the user read the report, they’d know that the news organisation wasn’t promoting its own opinions but a reference made by Union Minister Smriti Irani in 2016.
The use of direct quotes itself hints that the statement was not made by The Wire.
The article dates back to February 27, 2016, after the former HRD Minister’s Lok Sabha speech addressing the criticism of the government’s handling of the protests at JNU by alleging that “anti-national” events were held on campus.
She made the speech on February 24, 2016, and the relevant portion can be watched 31:40 minutes onward.
Irani claimed that the excerpt on Durga Puja was printed on a pamphlet for the celebrations of the ‘Mahishasur Martyrdom Day’ in 2014 which was denied by the organisers of the event.
JNU student Anil, a member of All India Backward Students’ Forum (AIBSF), who was one of the organisers, told The Wire, “What Irani said was totally fabricated.

An excerpt from an article in The Wire is making the rounds on Twitter to claim that the news organisation promoted ‘anti-Hindu’ sentiments by terming Durga Puja a “racist festival” and the Hindu deity a “sex worker”.
Ex-navy officer Harinder Sikka questioned The Wire in a critically worded tweet, “Can u dare write such obscene words for Islam?”
Twitter handle @missionkaali followed by Delhi BJP leader Kapil Mishra also shared the screenshot speculating if the outlet indeed published the excerpt.
Several other users — @Voice_Of_Dharma, @Muralik79739498 — posted the screenshot. Twitter handle @indianrightwing opined, “Maa durga being called a s*x worker that too during navratri by
@thewire_in. There can be no punishment except for legal death sentence…”
Twitter handle @indianrightwing which suggested the “death penalty” for The Wire as punishment for alleged “Hinduphobic” views also shared the article containing the excerpt in question.
Had the user read the report, they’d know that the news organisation wasn’t promoting its own opinions but a reference made by Union Minister Smriti Irani in 2016.
The use of direct quotes itself hints that the statement was not made by The Wire.
The article dates back to February 27, 2016, after the former HRD Minister’s Lok Sabha speech addressing the criticism of the government’s handling of the protests at JNU by alleging that “anti-national” events were held on campus.
She made the speech on February 24, 2016, and the relevant portion can be watched 31:40 minutes onward.
Irani claimed that the excerpt on Durga Puja was printed on a pamphlet for the celebrations of the ‘Mahishasur Martyrdom Day’ in 2014 which was denied by the organisers of the event.
JNU student Anil, a member of All India Backward Students’ Forum (AIBSF), who was one of the organisers, told The Wire, “What Irani said was totally fabricated.
